sentences.text: Mullerornis modestus stands as the only species within this extinct genus.
This elephant bird stood 1.49 meters tall and weighed roughly 80 kilograms.
It was an extinct elephant bird native to Madagascar.
Its eggs were significantly smaller than those of Aepyornis, weighing about 0.86 kilograms.
Scientists formally described the genus in 1894.
The name honors Georges Muller, a French explorer who died in 1892.
Isotopic analysis suggests the animal was a browsing herbivore.
The size of its optic lobes implies it was likely nocturnal, though it may have also been active during twilight.
The genus belongs to the order Struthioniformes and the family Aepyornithidae.
It lived during the Late Pleistocene to Holocene, from 0.129 to 0 million years ago.
Radiocarbon dating of a bone indicates it survived until approximately 1260 years before present.
